span.label: The core metabolic networks of 43 organisms across archaea, bacteria and eukaryota, as drawn from the WIT pathway-genome database.
span.quote: this database provides description for 6 archaea, 32 bacteria and 5 eukaryota

span.label: Is the topology of a metabolic network the homogeneous random kind predicted by Erdos-Renyi, or the heterogeneous scale-free kind found in the web and in social networks?
span.quote: Our first goal was to identify the structure of the metabolic networks, i.e., to establish if their topology is best described by the inherently random and uniform exponential model 21 (Fig. 1a and b), or the highly heterogeneous scale-free model 2 (Fig. 1c and d).

span.label: Shows that metabolic networks in all three domains of life are scale-free, and that their diameter is conserved across organisms of very different complexity - a property the non-biological scale-free networks do not have.
span.quote: A unique feature of metabolic networks, as opposed to that seen in non-biological scale-free networks, is the apparent conservation of the network diameter in all living organisms.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We show that, despite significant variances in their individual constituents and pathways, these metabolic networks display the same topologic scaling properties demonstrating striking similarities to the inherent organization of complex non-biological systems 2.

span.label: large-scale topology of metabolic networks
span.quote: Here we present the first systematic comparative mathematical analysis of the metabolic networks of 43 organisms representing all three domains of life.

span.label: computational-network-analysis
span.quote: To begin to address the large-scale structural organization of cellular networks, we have examined the topologic properties of the core metabolic network of 43 different organisms based on data deposited in the WIT database 19.

span.label: mechanisms
span.quote: the emergence of power law distribution is intimately linked to the growth of the network in which new nodes are preferentially attached to already established nodes 2

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: mechanisms

span.label: Eighteen of the 43 organisms are not fully sequenced and many ORFs are functionally unassigned, so the substrate and reaction lists analysed are incomplete.
span.quote: As 18 of the 43 organisms deposited in the database are not yet fully sequenced, and a substantial portion of the identified ORFs are functionally unassigned, the list of enzymes, and consequently the list of substrates and reactions (see Table 1 in Supplementary Material 26), will certainly be expanded in the future.

span.label: The extension of the conclusion to non-metabolic cellular networks is only preliminary, because those networks are too small for unambiguous statistical analysis with current tools.
span.quote: While the current mathematical tools do not allow unambiguous statistical analysis of the topology of other networks due to their relatively small size, our preliminary analysis suggest that connectivity distribution of non-metabolic pathways also follows a power-law distribution, indicating that cellular networks as a whole are scale-free networks.

span.label: The whole analysis rests on one predicted database, whose pathways are inferred from annotated genomes rather than observed.
span.quote: This integrated pathway-genome database predicts the existence of a given metabolic pathway based on the annotated genome of an organism combined with firmly established data from the biochemical literature.

span.label: Across 43 organisms from all three domains of life, metabolic networks share the SAME scale-free topology (power-law degree distribution) as non-biological complex networks — a common blueprint dominated by a few highly connected hubs.
span.quote: these metabolic networks display the same topologic scaling properties demonstrating striking similarities to the inherent organization of complex non-biological systems

span.label: Metabolic networks in all three domains of life are scale-free: the number of reactions a substrate takes part in follows a power law.
span.quote: our results convincingly indicate that the probability that a given substrate participates in k reactions follows a power-law distribution, i.e., metabolic networks belong to the class of scale-free networks

span.label: The network diameter is the same in all 43 organisms regardless of how many substrates they have - which is not what network growth predicts, and the paper calls it unprecedented.
